severity_criteria.source_excerpt: 5.1 Inclusion Criteria, criteria 4 and 5: "4." "Participants with an IGA score:" "VC period: 2 to 3 at screening and baseline" "5." "Participants with %BSA (excluding scalp) of AD involvement:" "VC period: 3% to 20% at screening and baseline" "The IGA is an overall eczema severity rating on a 0 to 4 scale that will be assessed during site" "0 Clear No erythema or induration/papulation, no oozing/crusting; there may be minor" "3 Moderate There may be pink-red erythema with moderate induration/papulation and there" -- The protocol gives inclusive ranges in prose (IGA 2 to 3 and BSA 3% to 20%); each endpoint is represented as its own threshold. Criterion 4 is IGA and criterion 5 is BSA. The protocol's IGA scale is 0 to 4.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 5.1 Inclusion Criteria 6; 6.6.1 and 6.6.3 Concomitant Medications and Procedures: "Participants who agree to discontinue all agents used to treat AD from screening through" "the final follow-up visit." "The following are permitted during the study:" " Participants may use bland emollients such as Eucerin® cream." " If sunscreen is needed, a mineral-based sunscreen (such as zinc oxide– or titanium" "oxide–based) with SPF of at least 30 may be used not less than 4 hours before and at" "least 2 hours after study drug application." " Participants may use nonsedating, over-the-counter antihistamines." "The following are not permitted during the study:" " Any investigational medication other than the study drug." " Topical corticosteroids, tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, and PDE4-inhibitors (Eucrisa®)." " Other topical agents for AD (except bland emollients as noted in Section 6.6.1)." " Treatment known to affect the course of AD." " Systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, cyclosporine A, azathioprine and biological" "therapies, or other immunosuppressant agents." " Allergen immunotherapy" " Phototherapy or tanning beds." -- The list separates explicit during-study prohibitions from prior-treatment washouts. Only medication and procedure restrictions from Section 6.6.3 are included as prohibited concomitant care; permission for bland emollients and listed allowed items is retained.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 5.1 Type I Error Control: "For the primary and key secondary endpoints, the overall 2-sided Type I error is 0.05." "A graphical procedure with gatekeeping testing strategy for the primary and key secondary" "analyses, as specified in Protocol Section 10.3, will be implemented to control the overall Type I" "error." "The underlying procedure is derived using the methodology developed in Bretz et al" "(2009)." "The method will guarantee a strong control of the family-wise error rate." "In Step 1, two families of 8 elementary hypotheses tests are grouped according to treatment" "• Family 1 (1.5% BID vs vehicle):" "• Family 2 (0.75% BID vs vehicle):" "To control the overall Type I error rate, 2-sided α = 0.05, the Bonferroni's method will be used." "In Step 1, within Family 1 and 2, the endpoints are tested in a fixed sequence at Bonferronized" "For any dose level, if the 4 related null hypotheses can" "If all null hypotheses in Family 1 and 2 are rejected, in Step 2, H31 and H32 will" "be tested using Bonferroni- Hochberg’s procedure with overall 2-sided α = 0.05 level." -- For this U.S. trial plan, a graphical gatekeeping procedure controls familywise error. The SAP reports a two-sided overall alpha of 0.05, fixed sequence testing within each dose family at 0.025, and later Bonferroni-Hochberg testing. The schema's testing_sequence cannot faithfully encode the two dose-specific families and conditional transitions, so it is left empty.

value.applies_to_period: during the study; safety follow-up follows study-treatment discontinuation
value.rationale: The protocol does not label these rules as rescue therapy. It prohibits additional AD agents and phototherapy during the study; when worsening AD requires a prohibited concomitant medication, study drug must be permanently discontinued. An EOT visit and safety follow-up are then required. Bland emollients are permitted.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 6.5.2 Criteria for Permanent Discontinuation; 6.6.3 Prohibited Medications and Procedures; 7.1.2 Discontinuation Procedures; 8.8 Safety Follow-Up: " Participant presents with a worsening of AD that requires treatment with a prohibited" "concomitant medication." "The following are not permitted during the study:" " Topical corticosteroids, tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, and PDE4-inhibitors (Eucrisa®)." " Other topical agents for AD (except bland emollients as noted in Section 6.6.1)." " Systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, cyclosporine A, azathioprine and biological" "therapies, or other immunosuppressant agents." " Phototherapy or tanning beds." " Participants may use bland emollients such as Eucerin® cream." " Participants must be followed for safety until the time of the follow-up visit or until" "follow-up period of the study for safety assessments." "visit, which should occur 30 (+ 7) days after the EOT visit (or after the last dose of study" "drug/treatment if the EOT visit was not performed." -- This records the protocol's explicit prohibition and discontinuation rules as rescue-related constraints; it does not assert a rescue agent, trigger threshold, or efficacy handling rule that the protocol does not state.

published_results.source_excerpt: 14.1 Atopic Dermatitis, Table 4 (TRuE-AD1 columns): "14 CLINICAL STUDIES 14.1 Atopic Dermatitis Adult and Pediatric Subjects 12 Years of Age and Older Two double-blind, randomized, vehicle-controlled trials of identical design (TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2, NCT03745638 and NCT03745651, respectively) enrolled a total of 1249 adult and pediatric subjects aged 12 and older, and subjects were treated twice daily (BID) for 8 weeks." "The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects at Week 8 achieving IGA treatment success (IGA-TS) defined as a score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with ≥ 2 grade improvement from baseline." "Efficacy results for OPZELURA from the two trials are summarized in Table 4." "Table 4: Efficacy Results at Week 8 in Adult and Pediatric Subjects 12 Years of Age and Older with Atopic Dermatitis (TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2) TRuE-AD1 TRuE-AD2 OPZELURA (N = 253) Vehicle (N = 126) Treatment Difference and 95% Confidence Interval OPZELURA (N = 228) Vehicle (N = 118) Treatment Difference and 95% Confidence Interval IGA-TS Defined as an IGA score of 0 or 1 with a ≥ 2-grade improvement from baseline 53.8% (136/253) 15.1% (19/126) 38.9% (30.3%, 47.4%) 51.3% (117/228) 7.6% (9/118) 44.1% (36.2%, 52.0%) Itch NRS (≥ 4 point reduction) (n/N) N = subjects with a baseline Itch NRS score ≥ 4." "52.2% (84/161) 15.4% (12/78) 36.7% (25.5%, 48.0%) 50.7% (74/146) 16.3% (13/80) 35.8% (24.4%, 47.2%) Pediatric Subjects 2 to 11 Years of Age A double-blind, randomized, vehicle-controlled trial, TRuE-AD3 (NCT04921969), enrolled a total of 330 pediatric subjects, 2 to 11 years of age, and subjects were treated twice daily (BID) for 8 weeks." -- Label Section 14.1 maps TRuE-AD1 to NCT03745638 and gives Week 8 Table 4 results by TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2. Rows here use the TRuE-AD1 columns only. The N=253 OPZELURA denominator maps to the 1.5% VC arm in base.json, and N=126 maps to the vehicle VC arm. Itch NRS uses the table's baseline Itch NRS ≥4 subset denominators (161 and 78); no population enum in this schema expresses that subset, so analysis_population is null. The label specifies the Itch assessment at Week 8, while the matching registry endpoint title is the VC-period ≥4-point Itch NRS endpoint. The printed values are counts and percentages; no arm-level confidence intervals are entered from the treatment-difference columns.
